title: The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia that aims at advancing co-operation in military, economic, cultural and energy affairs
author: PTI
content_html:
India and the four-member Visegrad group of Central European countries on Monday (September 21, 2026) agreed to step up political, economic and defence cooperation at their first Foreign Ministers' meeting, which External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar described as a “new historic occasion”.

The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia that aims to advance cooperation in military, economic, cultural, and energy affairs.

The first meeting between the Foreign Ministers of the Visegrad Group and India was held on Monday (September 21, 2026), on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.

Mr Jaishankar met with Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Radek Sikorski; Hungary's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Anita Orban; Slovakia's Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Juraj Blanar; and the Czech Minister of Foreign Affairs, Petr Macinka.

"It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion,” Mr. Jaishankar said in remarks after the meeting.

"It was a very, very productive meeting. What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4 we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum,” he said, adding that there was “consensus" that the Foreign Ministers of the five nations in the group would meet annually.

“We would also explore technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defence. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation,” Mr. Jaishankar said.

The group also discussed issues including space, connectivity, and people-to-people mobility.

Mr. Jaishankar said the meeting was “very worthwhile” and “very productive”, with discussions focusing on cooperation as well as major global crises, including the Ukraine conflict and developments in the Gulf.

“It was really a very, very worthwhile, very productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it,” he said in remarks to reporters after the meeting.

In a post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said the first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to closer political cooperation, including annual meetings of foreign ministers, and deeper economic cooperation, including the Annual Business Forum.

✅ Closer political cooperation including… pic.twitter.com/mBqMTkC6QN

— Dr. S. Jaishankar (@DrSJaishankar) September 21, 2026

The countries also agreed to strengthen technology, innovation, research and education partnerships; reinvigorate defence cooperation; further develop cultural cooperation and people-to-people relations and work together to support multilateralism, he said.

Mr. Jaishankar also said that India has “very good” relations with the V4 countries.

"These are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. These are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent, and I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work with the V4 together,” he told reporters.

title: Class 10 girl and boy returning from coaching groped and assaulted in Bihar’s Jamui, sparking a political row
author: Amarnath Tewary
content_html:
Two Class 10 students, a girl and a boy, returning from a coaching class, were allegedly groped and harassed by a group of men in Bihar’s Jamui district on Saturday (September 19, 2026). A video of the incident went viral on social media on Monday (September 21, 2026), prodding the police to register an FIR and arrest three people.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders said the incident was “deeply disturbing”, indicative of patriarchal attitudes among supporters of the ruling BJP, and exposing the State’s law-and-order situation.

The National Commission for Women on Monday (September 21, 2026) took suo motu cognisance of the alleged assault and harassment, and directed the Director General of Police to immediately file an FIR in the matter. The State Commission for Women also took suo motu cognisance of the incident, and promised that strict action would be taken against those found guilty.

Three arrested so far

“There was no formal complaint registered by anyone against anyone in the incident,” said Jamui Superintendent of Police Vishwajit Dayal. “The police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and approached the victim girl and her friend, a boy. Both were returning from a hillside area after their coaching was over on the Jamui-Lakhisarai road where a group of six to seven people, some even masked, stopped them as it is shown in the viral video and they were being harassed on September 19 evening at around 7 p.m.,” he added.

An FIR (No 428/ 2026) was lodged in the incident at Jamui police station. All the people seen in the viral video were taken into custody and three of them have been arrested. “The police will soon arrest all of those found involved in this unfortunate incident,” Mr. Dayal said.

Register FIR, stop sharing video: NCW

“Any compromise on the dignity, safety, and privacy of women is unacceptable at any level,” said the NCW. The Commission’s chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to the Bihar DGP, directing him to immediately register an FIR in the incident. The NCW also directed that security, legal assistance, and psychological counselling be provided to the victims, seeking a detailed Action Taken Report in the matter. All necessary legal action should also be taken to stop further sharing of the objectionable video being circulated on social media, the NCW directed.

The Bihar State Commission for Women also took suo motu cognisance of the incident. “I’ve spoken to the Jamui officials, and they detailed to me about the incident as it happened on September 19 evening at 7 p.m. Stern action will be taken against all those found involved in this incident by people having a weird mindset. The Bihar State Commission for Women stands with all such hapless women,” Commission chairperson Apsara said.

‘When control is mistaken for culture’

“The video from Jamui is deeply disturbing,” Mr. Gandhi said in a social media post. “Two class 10 students were stopped on a road. Harassed. Humiliated. Molested. A young girl’s hands folded, begged to be let go while goons groped her and dragged her away. This is not ‘culture’. It is patriarchy: the belief that any man can police a girl’s body, her movement, her choice… When control is mistaken for culture, and such attitudes are normalised by ‘Andhbhakts’, mobs start believing they are the law,” he added.

Demanding prosecution of the culprits under the POCSO Act, Mr. Gandhi, who is also Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha asked, “Who gave these men the right to behave like this? The Bihar government must answer why a girl is not safe on a public road at 7 p.m.?”

Recalling the Jamui and Delhi rape and murder incidents, the Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge too demanded the “harshest punishment for culprits, and accountability from State governments”. Such incidents, he said, “scream to expose the lies and hypocrisy of the BJP’s ‘Nari Shakti Vandan’ and ‘Beti Bachao’ schemes”, meant to empower women.

‘Extremely shameful’

Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav, Leader of Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, also slammed the State government in a social media post.

“Bihar has been shamed by the BJP-NDA government. Everyone is ashamed. On the Jamui incident, the government’s people are making low-level statements… When the Jamui incident happened, [Bihar Chief Minister] Samrat Choudhary was holding a caste conference,” he noted.

His Singapore-based sister Rohini Acharya said: “The incident in Jamui is extremely shameful and expresses the dire state of law and order under the Samrat government, along with lax administrative influence and the stark reality of policing.” She alleged that the “sisters and daughters of the State are entirely unsafe”.

RJD leader and former MLA Shakti Singh Yadav said, “The law and order situation has completely collapsed in the State, but the government keeps drum beating that women in Bihar today can safely travel even at midnight.”

‘Guilty will be behind bars soon’

State Rural Works Minister Sunil Kumar, said that he too has spoken to the Jamui Superintendent of Police and got all the details about the incident. “All those people allegedly involved into the incident would be behind bars very soon… The Jamui incident even was raked up at the government level,” said Mr. Kumar, who has earlier been a senior police official in the State.

His State Cabinet colleague and Bihar Sports Minister Shreyasi Singh is the BJP MLA from Jamui. “Victims had not filed the FIR, police did it after the viral video and three people have been arrested, the rest too will be arrested…I’m satisfied with the administrative action and hope they will continue to do so.”

(with inputs from Sreeparna Chakrabarty in New Delhi)

title: Google to report child abuse content directly to Indian authorities
author: Reuters
content_html:
Google said on Monday (September 22, 2026) it has agreed to report content flagged as ​child sexual abuse material to Indian authorities, breaking from a ‌global practice under which such reports are first ​routed through a U.S. non-profit.

The decision follows ⁠a similar announcement by Meta last week. It comes after two Indian government sources told Reuters they had in recent weeks ‌pressed tech companies like Google and Microsoft to report child abuse content concerning India directly, given ‌concerns that the existing system delays reports significantly.

A ‌Google ⁠spokesperson said the company “invests significantly to detect, deter, ⁠remove, and report child sexual abuse material,” and described the proposal as part of the company’s “ongoing discussions with the government of India.”

India ​is the largest market ‌by users for both Meta’s Facebook and Google’s YouTube, and Meta’s own shift followed weeks of friction with the Indian government, including an apology last month by ‌CEO Mark Zuckerberg over the spread of child ​sexual abuse material on the company’s platforms.

Meta and Alphabet Inc’s Google have for years ⁠made such reports to the U.S.-based National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, which then relays reports to law enforcement in ‌the country involved.

Indian officials had argued to tech platforms that the arrangement costs precious time in cases where a child may be in active danger, since reports pass through that intermediary before reaching domestic police who can act on the ground, according to two ‌sources.

Child sexual abuse material remains a vast and growing global problem. ​The CyberTipline, run by that same nonprofit, received more than 21.3 million reports from around ⁠the world of suspected child sexual exploitation in 2025. Technology ⁠and law enforcement officials in the United States, the European Union and elsewhere have pushed platforms to ‌speed up detection and reporting, though most countries continue to route reports through the U.S. nonprofit ​as the primary international clearing house.

title: Survey discovers six new species from Periyar Tiger Reserve in Keralam
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Highlighting the rich biodiversity of the Periyar Tiger Reserve (PTR) in Keralam’s Thekkady, a four-day faunal survey recorded six species previously undocumented in the reserve, including one bird, one butterfly, and four odonate species.

According to officials, the newly recorded bird species is the golden-headed cisticola (Cisticola exilis). A total of 174 bird species were documented during the exercise, raising the reserve’s cumulative bird count to 347.

The survey also recorded the common onyx butterfly (Horaga onyx). With 192 butterfly species sighted during the four-day event, the total number of documented butterfly species in the reserve has risen to 284.

Common onyx butterfly (Horaga onyx). | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

Odonate species

Additionally, four odonate species (dragonflies and damselflies) were recorded in the reserve for the first time: the parakeet darner (Gynacantha millardi), fraser’s clubtail (Acrogomphus fraseri), spiny horntail (Burmagomphus chaukulensis), and nilgiri clawtail (Lamelligomphus nilgiriensis). With 68 odonate species documented in total, the consolidated odonate checklist for PTR now stands at 111.

Spiny horntail (Burmagomphus chaukulensis). | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

Beyond birds, butterflies, and odonates, the composite assessment documented 15 mammal, 30 spider, 34 ant, and five cicada species.

Kalesh Sadasivan, research associate of the Travancore Nature History Society (TNHS) noted that the golden-headed cisticola is a rare species typically found at higher elevations. He added that the findings reflect the importance of the reserve’s elevational gradient, evergreen forests, grasslands, and ecotonal habitats in supporting diverse wildlife assemblages.

“The healthy ecosystem and unpolluted water bodies in PTR are behind these new records. Surveys have been conducted regularly over the last decade, consistently documenting new additions,” Dr. Sadasivan said.

Necessity of surveys

P.P. Pramod, field director of PTR, stated that adding six new distribution records to an area as intensively studied as Periyar highlights the necessity of systematic biodiversity surveys. “These studies help us understand changes in species distribution and habitat use, strengthening the evidence base for long-term conservation management,” he said.

“The survey covered widely separated camps representing varied elevations, habitats, and levels of accessibility,” said Periyar East division deputy director Midhun Mohan.

Fraser’s clubtail (Acrogomphus fraseri). | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT

Held from September 10 to 13, the survey was a collaborative effort involving 75 delegates from 21 NGOs, academic and research institutions, along with Forest department officials and frontline staff. Participants were organised into 21 teams deployed across 20 active base camps to cover all major ecological zones of the tiger reserve.
